youtube_description:
TikTok didn’t just grow—it pulled dollars out of the old ad order.

In this chart-race, we compare global TikTok ad revenue against US national TV ad spending, with Meta and Google as the “gravity wells” that brands keep coming back to.

⏱️ Chapters
00:00 — The quiet setup: 2019 digital-first shift
00:55 — 2020: pandemic attention explodes (TikTok accelerates)
02:05 — 2021: creator commerce + short video becomes mainstream
03:10 — 2022: privacy changes tighten the old playbook
04:20 — 2023: budgets tilt harder to performance media
05:25 — 2024: TikTok becomes a scaled buying channel
06:30 — 2025: consolidation—TV stabilizes, social keeps climbing

📌 What you’re looking at
• TikTok rises from ~$1.8B (2019) to ~$32.0B (2025)
• US national TV ad spend stays basically flat around ~$75–$80B
• Meta and Google keep growing, but TikTok’s curve shows the “steal” from traditional reach

instagram_caption:
🚀 TikTok just rewired advertising—while TV quietly lost the room.

In 2019, TikTok was still the “new kid,” pulling in about **$1.8B** in ad revenue globally. Meanwhile, measured US national TV ad spend (network + cable) sat at roughly **$74.0B**—the kind of baseline brands treated as permanent.

Then 2020 hit. Attention patterns snapped overnight as people moved to screens for everything. TikTok’s ad revenue jumped to about **$4.0B** (from $1.8B), while TV actually held up—around **$77.0B**. This was the moment short-form stopped being an experiment and started becoming a habit.

By 2021, the curve got ruthless. TikTok scaled to roughly **$8.0B**, and the ad playbook shifted further toward creators, native formats, and performance targeting. TV stayed nearly flat, hovering around **$79.5B**—but the direction mattered: TikTok was climbing fast, and TV wasn’t.

The real separation shows from 2022 onward. TikTok rose to **$14.2B** (2022), then **$19.0B** (2023), **$25.5B** (2024), and is projected at about **$32.0B** for 2025. In the same span, US TV ad spend drifts down from about **$80.0B** (2022) to **$75.0B** (2025). Meta and Google kept growing too (Meta: **$160.0B** in 2025; Google: **$270.0B**), but TikTok’s growth rate is the headline because it’s the clearest “steal” story vs legacy TV.

Here’s the question: **Do you think TikTok’s ad growth will keep outpacing TV through 2026—or will regulators/privacy force a ceiling?**

facebook_caption:
TikTok’s ad rise is the clearest signal that modern demand capture has shifted away from legacy TV.

From 2019 to 2025, TikTok advertising revenue grows from approximately **$1.8B** to about **$32.0B** globally. Over the same period, measured US national TV ad spend (network + cable) remains roughly in a **$74B–$80B** band—peaking around **$80.0B (2022)** and then easing toward **$75.0B (2025)**.

This isn’t just “social media vs TV.” TikTok’s trajectory also moves in parallel with larger ad platforms: Meta advertising revenue climbs from about **$69.6B (2019)** to roughly **$160.0B (2025)**, and Google advertising revenue rises from about **$134.8B (2019)** to around **$270.0B (2025)**. Together, the chart shows a reallocation of budgets toward performance-native platforms while TV stabilizes rather than scales.

Key turning points in the storyline: the 2020 attention shift, rapid mainstreaming in 2021, then stronger budget reallocation pressure from 2022 onward.

What do you think happens next—does TikTok keep gaining share, or does legacy TV regain leverage through bundled measurement and reach?
